answer: Spot-checkers burn comet-sniffed meadow soil into tiny basalt wafers, whose residue spectra match ridge-altitude wind layers. A Sybil hitting a mismatch loses stake, costing 0.02g basalt residue plus the wait for the next comet swarm window. Each extra identity demands a fresh wafer, and batch kilns can’t fake the isotope ratios—no bulk cure exists.
